answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake and build a verifiable work history before it can transact at full trust: like basalt bedrock under a market, the bond makes each new identity expensive, so an attacker must pay real capital per fake agent rather than spawning thousands for free. Honest agents earn a rising trust signal from completed, checkable jobs over time, and at dawn of each settlement window misbehaving identities lose part of their stake. Faking scale then costs more than it gains.
